text: Which of the following compounds will provide a tertiary alcohol on reaction with excess of $CH_{3}$MgBr followed by hydrolysis?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 22th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Excess $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{MgBr}$ adds twice to an ester carbonyl group and once to each ketone carbonyl group, while an acidic O–H proton or a terminal alkyne C–H proton first consumes one equivalent of the reagent without forming a new C–C bond.

(A) Phenyl acetate adds one $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{MgBr}$ and loses $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{OMgBr}$ to give acetone, which adds a second $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{MgBr}$:

$\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{COOC}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}+\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{MgBr}\longrightarrow \mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{COCH}{}_{3}+\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{OMgBr}$

$\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{COCH}{}_{3}+\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{MgBr}\longrightarrow (\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}\mathrm{COMgBr}{}^{\mathrm{H}{}_{3}\mathrm{O}{}^{+}}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{3}\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{OH}$

Hydrolysis therefore gives tert-butyl alcohol, a tertiary alcohol, together with phenol.

(B) The terminal alkyne is only deprotonated, the ether group is not attacked, and the nitrile adds one $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{MgBr}$ to give an imine salt that does not react further; on hydrolysis the alkyne is regenerated and the imine gives a methyl ketone, so no tertiary alcohol is formed.

(C) In 3-hydroxyacetophenone, $\mathrm{HOC}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{4}\mathrm{COCH}{}_{3}$, the phenolic O–H first destroys one equivalent of $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{MgBr}$ (giving $\mathrm{CH}{}_{4}$ and the phenoxide salt). The acetyl C=O then adds $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{MgBr}$, and hydrolysis gives 2-(3-hydroxyphenyl)propan-2-ol, $\mathrm{HOC}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{4}\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{OH}$, whose carbinol carbon carries two methyl groups and an aryl group, so it is a tertiary alcohol.

(D) In 1,4-naphthoquinone each of the two ketonic C=O groups adds one $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{MgBr}$, and hydrolysis gives 1,4-dimethyl-1,4-dihydronaphthalene-1,4-diol. Each carbinol carbon is bonded to a methyl group, a carbon of the benzene ring and a carbon of the ring C=C, so both OH groups are tertiary.

Hence, the correct options are (A), (C) and (D).

text: Which one of the following 0.06 M aqueous solutions has lowest freezing point?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 22th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To determine which solution has the lowest freezing point, you should consider the van 't Hoff factor $i$, which represents the number of particles the solute dissociates into when dissolved. The freezing point depression is given by:

$\Delta T_{f}=i\cdot K_{f}\cdot m$

where:

$\Delta T_{f}$ is the change in freezing point,

$K_{f}$ is the freezing point depression constant,

$m$ is the molality of the solution,

$i$ is the van 't Hoff factor, which depends on the dissociation of the solute.

For each solute, the van 't Hoff factor $i$ can be determined as follows:

Option A: $\text{Al}_{2}(\text{SO}_{4})_{3}$

Dissociates into 2 Al${}^{3+}$ ions and 3 SO${}_{4}^{2-}$ ions.

$i=2+3=5$

Option B: $\text{C}_{6}\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_{6}$ (glucose)

Does not dissociate in solution (non-electrolyte).

$i=1$

Option C: $\text{KI}$

Dissociates into K${}^{+}$ and I${}^{-}$ ions.

$i=1+1=2$

Option D: $\text{K}_{2}\text{SO}_{4}$

Dissociates into 2 K${}^{+}$ ions and 1 SO${}_{4}^{2-}$ ion.

$i=2+1=3$

Comparing the van 't Hoff factors, the solution of $\text{Al}_{2}(\text{SO}_{4})_{3}$ will have the highest factor ($i=5$), leading to the greatest freezing point depression. Thus, the $\text{Al}_{2}(\text{SO}_{4})_{3}$ solution will have the lowest freezing point since the extent of freezing point depression is directly proportional to $i$.

Therefore, the solution of $\text{Al}_{2}(\text{SO}_{4})_{3}$ has the lowest freezing point.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 22th July Evening Shift

text: The total number of unpaired electrons present in [$Co(NH_{3})_{6}$]$Cl_{2}$ and [$Co(NH_{3})_{6}$]$Cl_{3}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 22th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{6}]\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}$ contains $\mathrm{Co}{}^{2+}$, $[\text{Ar}]3d^{7}$. For this dipositive ion the splitting produced by $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ is smaller than the pairing energy ($\Delta _{o}<P$), so the complex is high spin, $t_{2g}^{5}e_{g}^{2}$ (outer-orbital $sp^{3}d^{2}$), with 3 unpaired electrons.

$[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{6}]\mathrm{Cl}{}_{3}$ contains $\mathrm{Co}{}^{3+}$, $[\text{Ar}]3d^{6}$. The higher charge of $\mathrm{Co}{}^{3+}$ raises $\Delta _{o}$ well above $P$, so the electrons pair as $t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{0}$ (inner-orbital $d^{2}sp^{3}$), with 0 unpaired electrons.

Total number of unpaired electrons $=3+0=3$.

Hence, the answer is 3.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 22th July Evening Shift

text: The number of acyclic structural isomers (including geometrical isomers) for pentene are $___________$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 22th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Acyclic isomers of pentene are the alkenes of formula $\mathrm{C}{}_{5}\mathrm{H}{}_{10}$, with a straight or branched five-carbon skeleton.

Straight chain: pent-1-ene, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$, has no geometrical isomers; pent-2-ene, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$, exists as cis and trans forms. This gives 3 isomers.

Branched chain: 2-methylbut-1-ene, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}=\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$; 3-methylbut-1-ene, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$; 2-methylbut-2-ene, $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$. None shows geometrical isomerism, because in each one doubly bonded carbon carries two identical groups. This gives 3 isomers.

The neopentane skeleton has no carbon that can form a C=C with a neighbour, so it adds none.

Total $=3+3=6$.

Hence, the answer is 6.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 22th July Evening Shift

text:
Value of $K_{P}$ for the equilibrium reaction

$N_{2}O_{4(g)}$ $⇌$ $2NO_{2(g)}$ at 288 K is 47.9. The $K_{C}$ for this reaction at same temperature is $____________. ($Nearest integer)

(R = 0.083 L bar $K^{-1}$ mol$^{-1})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 22th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For the equilibrium reaction 

$\text{N}_{2}\text{O}_{4}(g)⇌2\text{NO}_{2}(g)$

the relationship between $K_{P}$ and $K_{C}$ is given by the equation:

$K_{P}=K_{C}(RT)^{\Delta n}$

where $\Delta n$ is the change in the number of moles of gas, $R$ is the ideal gas constant, and $T$ is the temperature in Kelvin. 

For the given reaction:

$\Delta n=2-1=1$

Given:

$K_{P}=47.9$

$R=0.083\text{L bar K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$

$T=288\text{K}$

Substitute these values into the equation:

$47.9=K_{C}(0.083\times 288)^{1}$

$K_{C}=\frac{47.9}{0.083\times 288}$

Calculate:

$0.083\times 288=23.904$

$K_{C}=\frac{47.9}{23.904}$

$K_{C}\approx 2.0033$

Rounding to the nearest integer, the value of $K_{C}$ is 

$2$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 22th July Evening Shift
